newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Fidel Velazquez could return to work -CTM.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Fidel Velazquez could return to work -CTM.

text.p: Powerful Mexican labour boss Fidel Velazquez, recovering from an intestinal infection that has kept him off the job for 40 days, may return to work on Tuesday, a labour leader said on Monday.

Velazquez, who turns 97 on Thursday, is the longtime chief of the six-million-strong Mexican Workers Confederation (CTM). He is credited with swinging Mexican workers behind the government for decades.

Velazquez "is doing well, but he's not eating what he should because he is very weak...maybe tomorrow (Tuesday) the doctor will allow him to come in for a little while", Leonardo Rodriguez, head of the CTM in Velazquez's absence, told a news conference.
Rodriguez said Velazquez has kept abreast of CTM matters during his absence, which included two stays in the hospital.
Velazquez would attend the CTM's May Day celebration on May 1, Rodriguez said.
